Y1115.claim: `\|w[u] - w[v]\|` telescopes: summed along a path it collapses to a function of the endpoints
Y1115.method: lead recheck: derivation check (constructed counterexample) plus measurement (`scripts/r9/round6.out`)
Y1115.evidence: The telescoping step is stated without its qualifier and is false as written. It holds only on paths monotone in `w`: for node weights w = 0, 10, 0 the summed term is 10 + 10 = **20** while the endpoint difference is **0**, so the sum is not a function of the endpoints. The conclusion the step supports is nevertheless measured and correct — `round6.py` gives "shipped: goods with an alternative optimum 1 of 29 (paper); structured: 11 of 29". The argument needs "along a monotone path", or a cancellation argument that does not assume telescoping.

Y447.claim: Cost per good is one uncapacitated min-cost flow on 80 nodes and 318 arcs plus an O(V+E) sweep
Y447.method: lead recheck: file read (`scripts/drain.py` L203-260 `sweep_priority`, L276-297 `run_drain`, L143-165 `sweep`) plus arithmetic check on the flow sizing
Y447.evidence: The flow sizing is right: 80 nodes and 2 x 159 = 318 arcs (`flowop.ARCS`). The sweep complexity is not, for the code that actually runs. `run_drain`'s default is `deterministic=True` (L276), which calls `sweep_priority` (L290) — a Kahn sweep with a `heapq` priority ready-queue (L209 `import heapq`, L232 `heapq.heappush`, L236 `heapq.heappop`), i.e. **O((V+E) log V)**; its stall branch additionally scans all of `core` (L240). The non-default `sweep` (L143) is a scan-order loop, O(V^2) worst case. Neither path is O(V+E). The practical point — the LP dominates the cost — is unaffected.
